title: [C15T4] - Anthropology graduates
prompt: The chart below shows what Anthropology graduates from one university did after finishing their undergraduate degree courses. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The pie chart illustrates the career destinations of Anthropology graduates from one university after completing their undergraduate studies, while the table shows the salary distribution of those in employment five years after graduation across different sectors.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, the majority of graduates entered full-time employment immediately after graduation, while unemployment rates remained relatively low. Additionally, government sector workers achieved the highest proportion of top-tier salaries after five years in the workforce.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding career destinations, more than half of the graduates (52%) secured full-time work directly after completing their studies. Part-time employment accounted for 15% of graduates, while a smaller proportion (5%) combined part-time work with postgraduate study. Those pursuing full-time postgraduate study represented 8% of graduates. The remaining graduates were either unemployed (12%) or their destinations were unknown (8%).

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Looking at salary progression after five years, government sector employees enjoyed the most favorable income distribution, with half earning over $100,000 annually and 30% in the $75,000-99,999 bracket. Freelance consultants showed a similarly strong earning pattern, with 40% achieving salaries above $100,000 and another 40% earning between $75,000-99,999. In contrast, private company employees demonstrated a more varied salary spread, with 30% earning the highest salaries, 25% in the upper-middle range, and a significant 35% earning between $50,000-74,999, which was notably higher than the other sectors in this bracket.
